text:
maria: Quick proposal: simplify the memory ownership surface by introducing an opaque Backing object that wraps residency + eviction hints. goal is to decouple allocator responsibilities from eviction logic. RFC here: https://redwood.internal/rfc/backing-opaque (WIP)
kevin: Curious — does Backing own the physical pages or just the metadata?
tanvi: +1 to decoupling. We need clarity on migration semantics across nodes (vram -> host -> remote).
maria: Backing is primarily a logical handle. it can point to resident GPU pages, host-staging, or a remote blob. the runtime holds a Ref<Backing> and the evictor operates on Backing instances, not raw allocations.
oliver: How do we handle zero-copy tensor views? i worry about extra copy when evicting a slice.
maria: plan is to keep a small fastpath: if Backing has contiguous GPU pages and no active views, evictor performs page remap. otherwise fall back to copy-to-host. tradeoff: complexity vs worst-case copy cost.
kevin: What about pinned/staged allocations that are shared across tenants? need clear ACLs on Backing mutation.
tanvi: Also what about serialized KVS for remote Backings? we should store a compact descriptor for bloom filtering in cache.
maria: Good points. Proposal includes ownership flags: immutable, pinned, migratable, shared. ACLs enforced at the Backing layer. KVS descriptor is the Backing ID + residency vector (small bitset).
devon: Rollout concerns: we can't break existing allocator ABI. Suggest feature-flag rollout: new Backing wrapper behind a flag, integration tests, then flip for a single tenant on Dedicated for 1 week.
oliver: microbench plan? we should measure latency P50/P95 for small (32B tokens) and long (2k tokens) inference, and batch throughput with 8/16 batch sizes. include small-page churn scenario.
maria: agreed. Also add regression test harness: simulate many small tensors with random lifetimes and run the evictor stress test.
kevin: API sketch? maybe:
```
struct Backing {
  id: U64,
  residency: enum { GPU, HOST, REMOTE },
  flags: bitset,
  pin_count: AtomicU32,
  export_handle(): Option<RemoteRef>,
}
// allocators return BackingHandles instead of raw pointers
fn alloc(size) -> BackingHandle
```
maría: minor nit: use `residency_mask` instead of single enum to represent multi-residency during transitions.
tanvi: Edge-case: what if eviction fails due to OOM on host staging? need graceful degradation path (fallback model variant or QoS).
maria: proposal includes fallback policy hook: on host-staging OOM, runtime signals router to fallback to lower-memory model. also record telemetry error tag `evict_host_oom`.
devon: Can infra expose per-tenant budgets to the evictor? we'll need that to respect Dedicated quotas.
maria: yes, Backing carries tenant_id and the evictor consults quota service before demoting.
kevin: Backwards compatibility: wrap old Alloc with a Backing shim that points to existing pages. should be straight-forward.
oliver: one more: include cost model for remap vs copy (cycles + pci bandwidth) so admission can choose remap only when beneficial.
maria: adding a simple cost_estimate() API on Backing proposed.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: staging build 5961234600 for runtime/backing-refactor created by CI. link: https://ci.internal/build/5961234600
tanvi: timeline proposal: write RFC doc, unit tests + harness (2w), staging rollout behind flag (1w), tenant canary (1w), flip (1w) -> ~5-6 weeks.
devon: sounds reasonable. i'll draft rollout playbook and runbook for `evict_host_oom` incidents.
maria: thanks. i'll update the RFC with API sketch and perf plan. ping me for review before merge. :thumbsup:
